why: TANITAD_PROGRAMME.md §5 charter: 'Criteria completeness is enforced by machinery, not memory — we measurably failed to keep them complete by hand.' This file is the machine-readable registry every eval output is diffed against. A criterion may be PRESENT or REFUSED-with-a-reason; it may never be SILENTLY ABSENT.

three_states.PRESENT: the metric is in the artifact at one of its keys
three_states.REFUSED: the artifact's `refused` block names the criterion AND gives a reason — admissible, and becomes a WORK ITEM
three_states.ABSENT: neither — VIOLATION. This is the silent omission the doctrine forbids.

doctrine.families_never_pooled: The four families are reported per-family. A single composite hides the trade-off we are trying to see.
doctrine.ade_alone_is_incomplete: ADE stays, but an eval reporting ADE alone must not be presented as a result (PI, 2026-08-02, binding).
doctrine.estimator: paired episode-cluster bootstrap over val episodes (taniteval/ci.py)
doctrine.forbidden_estimator: overlapping_holdout_se — biases the point estimate bidirectionally, up to a sign flip
doctrine.tier_required: every artifact carries its tier; T0 is a WM diagnostic and is NEVER driving performance

applicability.why: A criteria check that scores PROFILING artifacts against DRIVING criteria reports a huge violation count that is pure noise — and a probe reporting the wrong scope is worse than no probe (the `df` trap, the Thor `free` trap, the cgroup `usage_in_bytes` trap). Scope is therefore decided BEFORE any criterion is evaluated, and an artifact whose kind cannot be determined is reported as UNKNOWN, never silently dropped and never counted as compliant.

in_scope_if_any.reason: refav1 per-arm schema (taniteval/tools/refav1_arm.py): the four families are nested PER ARM at arms.<arm>.four_families.*, so the top-level `four_families` marker never matched and every refav1 record read UNKNOWN_SCOPE — invisible to the census while carrying all four binding families. Only the `cl` planner arm is scored; see `arm_scoring`.

out_of_scope_if_any.reason: corpus census artifact, not an eval
clip-level dump, not a scored eval

leak_guards.why: For ANY head, ask whether its inputs at inference include something the label was derived from. Same family as the C6 confound and the REF-A I-JEPA leak (~80 % of val inside train).

guards.rule: Inference uses VISION ONLY. Labels may use ego/privileged data (PI, 2026-08-03, binding).
guards.note: An artifact must state what the model consumed at inference, or its number cannot be checked for this.

guards.rule: The goal path and the situation path stay information-disjoint at inference; a goal input must not carry the situation classifier's output in any form (PI, 2026-08-03, binding).
A route/goal head scoring near 1.0 must publish its echo test against its own input.
guards.note: 2026-09-05: the nav-compliance intervention pair (taniteval.nav_compliance) IS the behavioural echo test and satisfies this guard.
guards.refav1_note: ⭐ This is where refav1's route-head intervention pair belongs — NOT on strat.nav_compliance_ctrl_shuffle, which is the control for a BEHAVIOUR rate the record does not emit. `paired_true_minus_shuffled_accuracy` (refav1_arm.py:2223, taniteval.ci paired episode-cluster bootstrap) is the echo test the strat.route_goal note demands, and `_echo_caveat` (refav1_arm.py:2184) states the bijection in the artifact itself.

criteria.label: headline metrics reported against their trivial control(s)
criteria.note: ⭐ THE CRITERION THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THE PROGRAMME'S LARGEST MISREAD. A model number without its control is unreadable: MEASURED 2026-08-23, the T1 `stage-a-repaired · cl` arm reads 9.3697 m while its own hold-action control reads 0.4246 m on the SAME windows — the trivial baseline beat the model 22×. An artifact reporting only the model's value looks like a result. Controls: hold-v0 (go straight at the observed entry speed) and constant velocity. ⛔ A paired interval that excludes zero while favouring the FLOOR means the trivial baseline won — render that as LOST, never as a tie.
criteria.refav1_note: The anti-echo block IS the floor comparison for a refav1 arm: it carries holdv0_baseline (the strongest trivial control) with its verdict, and `refav1.trivial_profile` reports what fraction of each arm's own windows are trivial.

GATE_estimator_cluster_unit.rule: A NavSim artifact MUST declare `estimator.cluster_unit`. Until the unit is settled and PRE-REGISTERED, the only admissible interval is an explicit {status:UNAVAILABLE, reason, n}. ⛔ A bare point estimate with no interval block, or an interval computed with the episode-cluster bootstrap, FAILS.
GATE_estimator_cluster_unit.why: Our episode-cluster bootstrap does not transfer: NavSim resamples SCENE TOKENS, not episodes, and NavSim scenes are explicitly allowed to OVERLAP (PUB-DEVKIT docs/splits.md: 'NavSim splits contain overlapping scenes'). Resampling overlapping units as if independent understates the variance — the same family as overlapping_holdout_se, which biases the POINT ESTIMATE bidirectionally up to a sign flip. Inventing a CI here would reproduce a retracted defect on a borrowed benchmark.
GATE_estimator_cluster_unit.admissible_until_settled: UNAVAILABLE with a reason and n

GATE_ego_status_enforcement.rule: A NavSim artifact MUST carry `protocol.ego_status_enforcement` naming the MECHANISM by which the agent did not read ego status, and the evidence for it. ⛔ 'we did not use it' is an assertion, not enforcement, and FAILS.
GATE_ego_status_enforcement.why: MEASURED from the devkit: there is NO switch that removes ego status. `EgoStatus` (ego_velocity, ego_acceleration, ego_pose) is ALWAYS populated on AgentInput and nothing in the framework verifies an agent declined to read it — `SensorConfig` gates cameras and LiDAR only. Our vision-only rule (PI, 2026-08-03, binding) is therefore ours alone to enforce and evidence. This is the leak-guard question in a borrowed harness: an input that is present at inference is consumed unless something PREVENTS it.
acceptable_mechanisms: the agent never receives EgoStatus (zeroed/stripped at the adapter seam, asserted in a test)
an ablation showing the metric is unchanged when ego fields are randomised

GATE_modality_label.rule: A NavSim artifact MUST declare `protocol.sensor_set` and `protocol.setting` (e.g. 'front-camera-only, perception-free'). ⛔ Comparing our row against a multi-camera or perception-based row without both fields present FAILS.
GATE_modality_label.why: The leaderboard server records NO modality — only TEAM_NAME, AUTHORS, EMAIL, INSTITUTION, COUNTRY — so every 'camera-only' claim in the field is the authors', not the server's. MEASURED 2026-08-27 from the banked primary: Drive-JEPA's 93.7 PDMS headline uses 1024x256 stacking FRONT+LEFT+RIGHT, while its perception-free row uses the front camera only at 512x256. Comparing our single 256x640 front-camera arm against the 93.7 row would be a category error in our own favour's opposite direction — and comparing it against the perception-free ladder is legitimate. The label is what makes the difference visible.

comparable_ladder_perception_free_front_._source: PUB-PAPER Drive-JEPA (arXiv 2601.22032) Table 1, read from the banked PDF
comparable_ladder_perception_free_front_._note: This is TanitAD's comparable class: front-camera-only, perception-free (supervised solely by human trajectories, no perception annotations), entry rung 21M and top rung 307M — our scale band.

published_reference_numbers._evidence: PUB-PAPER, extracted by the EvalFlyWheel from the banked PDFs 2026-08-27
published_reference_numbers.drive_jepa_v1_PDMS_NOTE: ⛔ 93.7, NOT 93.3. The abstract and §1 both say 93.7; the 93.3 appears only in the paper's own NeurIPS checklist, where it misquotes its own abstract. Cite 93.7 and note the internal inconsistency if the figure is load-bearing.
published_reference_numbers._harness_pin: ⛔ v1 PDMS must come from the v1.1 BRANCH — `main` is v2 and its scorer is the EPDMS scorer, so 'v1 PDMS from main' silently computes a different metric. Neither paper states a devkit SHA, and the 2025-09-29 human-filter bugfix (issue #151) sits between v2.2 and now, so which side they are on is UNVERIFIED. Pin OUR SHA beside our number.

OFFICIAL_COLUMN.harness: autonomousvision/navsim @ <SHA> — the SHA is part of the column, not a footnote
OFFICIAL_COLUMN.why: ⛔ NavSim v2 carries TWO protocols both called 'EPDMS', roughly 30 POINTS APART: the method papers' single-stage navtest-EPDMS (~76-88) and the challenge's navhard-two-stage (~35-56). A single 'EPDMS' column lets them be read as one metric — precise about the wrong thing, which is the overlapping_holdout_se class exactly. The NavSim authors explicitly disown the navtest variant in print.
OFFICIAL_COLUMN.consequence_for_our_positioning: ⭐ MEASURED 2026-08-28 by the EvalFlyWheel from the banked PDF (arXiv 2601.22032), SEVEN probe terms all zero — 'navhard', 'nav hard', 'two_stage', 'two-stage', 'two stage', 'private_test', 'challenge': Drive-JEPA NEVER mentions navhard. Its 87.8 'EPDMS on v2' is therefore the navtest variant, NOT the challenge protocol. ⇒ a navhard number of ours is NOT comparable to Drive-JEPA's 87.8. The camera-only navhard bar to anchor against is DrivoR 56.3 EPDMS at ~40M params (privileged ceiling 56.6).
OFFICIAL_COLUMN.what_still_stands: Drive-JEPA's PERCEPTION-FREE ladder is PDMS on NavSim v1 (their Table 2, 'the first block is the perception-free setting'): LAW 83.8 / World4Drive 85.1 / Epona 86.1 / Drive-JEPA 89.0. That is a v1 PDMS claim and remains valid AS A v1 CLAIM — it must never be printed in an EPDMS column.

GATE_no_cross_protocol_comparison.rule: Every NavSim number MUST declare `protocol.navsim_protocol` from the closed set below AND the devkit SHA. ⛔ Placing two different protocols in one column, or comparing across them, FAILS — including implicitly, by omitting the tag.
GATE_no_cross_protocol_comparison.why: ~30 points separate two protocols wearing the same name. Untagged, our own leaderboard would merge them by accident — and a reader has no way to tell. Same family as navsim.modality_label: the number is only meaningful with the condition attached.

EPDMS_submetrics._formula: EPDMS = prod(NC,DAC,DDC,TLC) * ( sum_w(TTC,EP,HC,LK,EC) / 16 ); filter_m = 1.0 if the human also violated m, else m(agent)

NC.name: no at-fault collisions
NC.family_note: a decision OUTCOME, not decision quality — see _family_caveat

DAC.name: drivable area compliance
DAC.family_note: staying on the drivable topology is a route-level property

DDC.name: driving direction compliance
DDC.family_note: direction-of-travel against the lane graph — route-level

TLC.name: traffic light compliance
TLC.family_note: stop/go at a light is a tactical decision

TTC.name: time to collision within bound
TTC.family_note: maps onto our long.distance_keeping criterion directly

HC.name: history comfort
HC.family_note: ⛔ UNMAPPED — comfort is a separate axis from our four families

EC.name: extended comfort
EC.family_note: ⛔ UNMAPPED — comfort; also never human-filtered (injected downstream of the filter)

EPDMS_submetrics._family_caveat: ⭐ THE HONEST READING, and it is a finding rather than a mapping problem: EPDMS measures COMPLIANCE AND OUTCOMES, not DECISION QUALITY. Nothing in it corresponds to our tac.manoeuvre_decision (selected vs executed manoeuvre), tac.confusion, or strat.route_goal (goal-setting quality). NC and TLC are mapped to TACTICAL as the closest honest home, but a collision-free run is not evidence that the manoeuvre DECISION was right. ⇒ An EPDMS number does NOT satisfy the four-families rule. A NavSim artifact must still emit our families, or refuse them with reason and n.

nuscenes.licence_status: CONFLICT, UNRESOLVED: the paper states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial); the AWS Open Data registry lists 'Commercial'. Treat as RESEARCH-ONLY until written terms are obtained.

planning_openloop.THE_VERDICT: INADMISSIBLE as a TanitAD criterion or gate. Usable ONLY as a cited external-comparability row. Three measurements: (1) the averaging convention alone moves one VAD checkpoint 0.72 -> 1.22 m (+70 %) and FLIPS the UniAD/VAD ranking; (2) the ground-truth HUMAN trajectory scores 0.36-0.96 % collision - the metric's false-positive floor exceeds the published spread; (3) AD-MLP with no camera and no LiDAR ties a full perception stack. And VAD's 'high-level command' is computed from the GT future trajectory thresholded at +/-2 m and handed back as an input - OUR route-head echo defect, published as state of the art.

schema_note: Three artifact schemas are recognised: `taniteval.driving` (headline.* + a top-level `refused` block); `four_families` (ff_*.json, per-family blocks whose criteria decline inline via {status:UNAVAILABLE, reason, n}); and `refav1` (rec_*.json from taniteval/tools/refav1_arm.py, which nests a full four_families block PER ARM at arms.<arm>.four_families.* and adds a record-level `refav1` block for the protocol, the strategic/tactical declared heads and the trivial profile). All three refusal idioms are honest and all three are read. The refav1 records are the programme's only T1 driving artifacts; see `arm_scoring` for which arm is scored and why the other four are not.

registry_hygiene.why: A criterion whose keys resolve in NO artifact anywhere is far more likely a REGISTRY TYPO than a universal absence. This happened twice on 2026-08-23 (tac.confusion), and the second time it was published to the PI as 'the surviving universal gap'. The checker therefore reports UNRESOLVABLE separately from ABSENT, and a test pins that every criterion resolves in at least one real artifact.
registry_hygiene.rule: Adding a criterion means naming the key the EMITTER actually writes. Read the producing code, do not guess the name. If a metric is genuinely not emitted anywhere yet, set `not_yet_emitted: true` so the intent is explicit and the audit stays green.

release_gate.why: The PI asked (2026-08-23) to finalize the tests and criteria that must run at EVERY model release. This block names which registry criteria are release-blocking, so the gate and the census read one source.
advisory: regression vs the previous release (per family)
(all criteria are advisory per the PI ruling above)
release_gate.advisory_note: Advisory until two clean releases exist to compare — a regression gate with no trustworthy baseline manufactures false failures.
release_gate.cannot_rule_is_a_verdict: ⭐ A criterion that cannot decide at the configured settings must return CANNOT-RULE, loudly — never a silent PASS and never a perpetual INCONCLUSIVE. MEASURED precedent: the O6 rank gate could never rule (spectrum n=24 against a ceiling of 1024) and its silence was read as a pass for weeks.

PI_RULING_2026-08-28.ruling: THE RELEASE GATE DOES NOT BLOCK A RELEASE.
PI_RULING_2026-08-28.effect: Every criterion below is ADVISORY. The gate REPORTS; it never stops a release. It still returns PASS / FAIL / CANNOT-RULE per criterion and still exits non-zero on a FAIL so CI can surface it — but no human or process is required to stop on that signal.
PI_RULING_2026-08-28.what_does_NOT_change: ⛔ Advisory is about AUTHORITY, not about honesty. The gate must keep reporting a FAIL as a FAIL, at full strength and in the same words. Softening a verdict because it no longer blocks would destroy the only thing the instrument is for. In particular the floor comparison stays loud: a release whose trivial control beats it 22x is still reported as beaten, and CANNOT-RULE is still a verdict, never a silent pass.
PI_RULING_2026-08-28.rationale_recorded: The programme has research character and moves faster than a blocking gate would allow; the PI keeps the stop/go authority rather than delegating it to the instrument. The gate's value is that nothing ships UNMEASURED - not that it can veto.

advisory_all: all four families PRESENT or REFUSED-with-reason-and-n
release_gate.advisory_note_previous: Each is cheap, objective, and earned by a measured failure. ⛔ A T1 artifact is REQUIRED: T0 is a world-model diagnostic and a release may never be gated on it alone.
release_gate.exit_code_contract: non-zero exit on any FAIL is RETAINED so automation can surface it; the exit code is information, not an authority to stop.

arm_scoring.why: A refav1 record holds FIVE arms on the same 40 windows. Scoring all five would multiply every criterion count by five and would present three trivial CONTROLS and one T0 diagnostic as if each were a driving eval. The record is therefore scored ONCE, on the arm a capability claim may rest on.
arm_scoring.scored_arm_is: the planner arm — plan() at t0 with the TRUE nav token; the predictor consumes the planner's OWN actions; trajectory = unicycle(controls, measured v0). This is the only arm whose number is a claim about the model.

not_scored.ha: CONTROL — hold the last OBSERVED (a, kappa) for K steps. A baseline, not a result.
not_scored.ha0: CONTROL — constant velocity (a=0, kappa=0) at the measured v0. The strongest trivial baseline.
not_scored.ha0_ext: CONTROL — the echo control (constant (a0, kappa0) from the measured t0 state).
not_scored.ol: ⛔ T0. The RECORDED future integrated from v0 — the kinematic-contract control. NEVER driving performance (EVAL_DOCTRINE.md 2026-08-09), and reading it as such is the misread the tier stamp exists to prevent.

arm_scoring.consequence: The controls are not invisible: ctrl.floor_comparison is answered by the arm's own anti-echo/holdv0 block, which IS the comparison against those baselines. They are simply not scored as separate driving artifacts.
arm_scoring.if_the_scored_arm_changes: Changing `scored_arm` means re-prefixing every `arms.cl.` key below. The prefix is duplicated deliberately rather than templated, because the checker resolves literal dotted paths and a template would be a second thing to keep in sync.
arm_scoring.strategic_mapping: ⭐ The one non-obvious mapping, recorded so it is not re-derived: refav1's `refav1.strategic` block IS a strategic DECISION/ROUTE readout (route classification with confusion, per-class, kappa, CI, and nav_true / nav_shuffled / nav_zero interventions), so strat.decision and strat.route_goal read PRESENT from it. It is NOT nav-COMPLIANCE: that criterion scores emitted BEHAVIOUR against the command, and refav1 emits no such readout. Mapping route accuracy onto strat.nav_compliance would commit exactly the error that criterion was created to prevent — the route label is a bijection of the fed token (141/141) and cannot fail. The three nav_compliance criteria therefore resolve to the record's own strategic declination at `arms.cl.four_families.strategic` ({status: UNAVAILABLE, reason, n}) and read REFUSED — visible WORK ITEMS, not silent omissions and not false passes.

changelog.change: Recognise the refav1 per-arm schema. Adds the `arms.cl.four_families` in-scope marker, the `arms.cl.` key alternative for every criterion in all four families plus hygiene and the leak guards, the two refav1 tier paths, and the `arm_scoring` block recording that only the `cl` planner arm is scored.
changelog.why: MEASURED: every refav1 record read UNKNOWN_SCOPE — 'matches no in-scope or out-of-scope marker'. They are the programme's only T1 driving artifacts and they carry all four binding families, so the completeness machinery was blind to exactly the artifacts it exists for. Root cause: the marker and the criteria both named top-level `four_families`, while refav1 nests it per arm.
changelog.ships_with: tools/tests/test_criteria_check.py — refav1-shaped fixture with a deliberate-regression arm per family, plus the arm-scoping arm (deleting a family from a NON-scored arm must change nothing) and two-sided emitter pins. A guard that has never been shown to fail proves nothing.
changelog.also: tools/criteria_check.py: the forbidden-estimator exoneration list missed the wording '⛔ NOT overlapping_holdout_se' (it carried 'not used' and 'is not' but no bare 'not <token>'), so a disavowal in anti_echo.holdv0_baseline.estimator read as a live use — a false violation on all 13 records. Same class as the earlier 'NOT used' miss recorded in that function.
